name: b200
description: NVIDIA B200 (two GB100 dies, Blackwell, sm_100) at 1980 MHz: one Vortex core per SM, with tensor memory.

sources.NUM_CORES: 148 SMs across eight GPCs on the two dies, presented to software as one device (Microbenchmarking NVIDIA's Blackwell Architecture, arXiv 2512.02189, Sec. II)
sources.NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE_WIDTH, FET: 64 resident warps per SM for compute capability 10.0 (NVIDIA Blackwell Tuning Guide); 32-thread warps; 4 SM processing blocks, each with its own scheduler, as on Hopper (the sub-partition count tcgen05's 4 x 32 TMEM lane quarters follow)
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE: 1980 MHz, derived from NVIDIA's FP32 peak: HGX B200 lists 600 TFLOPS FP32 for 8 GPUs, 75 TFLOPS per GPU = 148 SMs x 128 FP32 lanes x 2 FLOP x 1.98 GHz. Third-party listings disagree (1830-1980 MHz), so the vendor peak decides
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: Compute capability 10.0 throughput per SM per clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9, arithmetic instructions): 128 FP32, 64 INT32 add, the same as 9.0, so the h100 split carries over: one ALU/FPU/LSU block per processing block with 16 INT32 and 32 FP32 lanes. NVIDIA publishes no LD/ST unit count for sm_100; Hopper's 8 per processing block is kept
sources.FP64: Not modelled: XLEN=32 leaves out the D extension. B200 runs FP64 at half the FP32 rate (64 per SM per clock, compute capability 10.0 table), but ML workloads do not use it
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 16 results per clock per SM for reciprocal, reciprocal square root and the 32-bit conversions (compute capability 10.0 table), 4 per processing block: 32 FPU lanes / 8
sources.NUM_TFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM for rcp, rsqrt, log2, exp2, sin, cos (compute capability 10.0 table)
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Demand-paged MMU, global and shared-memory atomics with atomicCAS, FP16 storage and conversion, and per-partition special-function units for the transcendentals (TFU), as on every NVIDIA GPU since Pascal
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE, TCU_*: Fifth-generation tensor cores: FP16/BF16, TF32, FP8, FP6/FP4, MXFP8/MXFP6/MXFP4 and NVFP4 block scaling, INT8 (no INT4), 2:4 sparsity (HGX B200 specifications; arXiv 2512.02189 Sec. IV). Vortex has no FP6 format; MX covers the block-scaled types it has
sources.TCU_FEDP2K: Twice Hopper's dense tensor rate per SM: B200 2.25 PFLOPS FP16 (HGX: 36 PFLOPS sparse for 8 GPUs, dense half) = 7678 FLOP/clock/SM at 148 SMs and 1.98 GHz, against H100's 989 TFLOPS = 3786 at 132 SMs. FEDP2K doubles the FEDP's K, which h100 leaves off
sources.TCU_WGMMA_ENABLE: Required by Vortex's tensor memory, which uses the WGMMA tile buffers and operand path (VX_define.vh, SimX tcu_unit.cpp). Warps never issue WGMMA in a TMEM build, so, as on sm_100, there is no warpgroup MMA instruction
sources.TCU_TMEM_ENABLE, TCU_TMEM_COLS: '512 columns and 128 rows per CTA, with each cell being 32-bits' on sm_100a (PTX ISA 9.7.18.1); arXiv 2512.02189 Sec. III-A. cta_group::2 pairs two SMs' 128-lane TMEMs for M=256; it does not widen one SM's. Vortex derives its lanes from the TCU blocks x WGMMA M (4 x 16 = 64 at NT=32), so a core implements the sm_100 cta_group::1 M=64 shape, not M=128; only the 512 columns are set here
sources.EXT_DXA_ENABLE: The Tensor Memory Accelerator is the DXA; Vortex's tensor memory also requires it
sources.EXT_TEX_ENABLE, EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_O: Off: a compute part, and no NVIDIA source describes texture units on B200
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE, DCACHE_SIZE: 228 KB maximum shared memory per SM in a 256 KB combined L1/shared pool, the same as Hopper (NVIDIA Blackwell Tuning Guide, compute capability 10.0)
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 32 banks of 4 B per clock, as every NVIDIA SM since Maxwell; Vortex banks are XLEN wide, 4 B at XLEN=32, so the count matches the part
sources.DCACHE_NUM_BANKS: NVIDIA publishes no L1 bandwidth for sm_100; Hopper's 128 B per clock (4 banks of the 32 B dcache word) is kept, as the L1/shared pool is unchanged
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS: 126 MB L2 (NVIDIA Blackwell Tuning Guide): 63 ways over 32768 sets of 64 B lines, the power-of-two set count h100 uses
sources.L2_NUM_BANKS: Four L2 partitions, double Hopper's (arXiv 2512.02189 Sec. II): twice h100's 64 banks
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 8 HBM3e stacks (arXiv 2512.02189 Sec. II) at 8 TB/s per GPU (DGX B200: 64 TB/s for 8 GPUs). Modelled as 64 HBM3 channel pairs of 16 B at 7813 MT/s = 8.0 TB/s; the enum has no HBM3e, as for h200
sources.L2_MSHR_SIZE: 256 per bank: Little's law on B200's L2-miss round trip (824 - 296 = 528 cycles) x 4040 B/cycle (8000 GB/s / 1980 MHz) / (128 banks x 64 B) = 260; 256 is the ceiling of the TOML's own derivation (98% of the requirement)
sources.reference: fp32_lanes = 148 SMs x 128 FP32 lanes; dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak (DGX B200). Latencies: Chips and Cheese, 'Nvidia's B200: Keeping the CUDA Juggernaut Rolling' (2025), OpenCL pointer chase on a B200: L1 19.61 ns ('19.6 ns, or 39 cycles'), L2 149.65 ns in the near L2 partition, DRAM 416.00 ns at 2 GB, at 1980 MHz = 39, 296 and 824 cycles. The same test gives H100 PCIe 154.69 and 377.64 ns, which at its 1755 MHz boost are within 1% of h100's references from arXiv 2507.10789, so the two sources agree. The far L2 partition (316.19 ns past 64 MB) is not modelled: Vortex has one L2
sources.L1_LINK_LATENCY, L2_LINK_LATENCY, PLATFO: 1, 102 and 445 core cycles, calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the one-core SimX pointer chase gives the B200's measured latencies in 'reference' (L1 37.9, L2 295.8, DRAM 823.7 cycles)
sources.xlen: 32-bit machine: NVIDIA's per-thread registers are 32 bits (64-bit values take register pairs), and Vortex TMEM cells are 32 bits, so tmem.ld needs no NaN-boxing. XLEN=32 also means no FP64 (the D extension follows XLEN=64; ML workloads do not use it) and a 32-bit device address space (4 GB, against the part's 49-bit virtual addresses); configure --profile picks a build32 tree and a build64 tree rejects the profile
